title: Zscaler API reads that withhold or mask a secret

prose.text: Withholding takes three forms here: the field is absent from the read, the value is masked, or there is no read operation at all.
{{zia-admin-password}} The Terraform resource follows the same contract: [[zia.terraform.admin-identity:admin-password-not-returned]].

{{sandbox-token-send-only}} {{sandbox-token-no-read}} The Python SDK does the same: [[zia.sdk-python.sandbox-client:zscsb-token-query-param]]; the token model is in [[shared.legacy-api.zia-session:sandbox-token]].
{{obfuscate-flag}} {{cloud-api-key-no-read}} The key is managed in the console: [[shared.legacy-api.zia-session:one-key]].
{{ba-cert-no-private-key}} The upload blob that carries the key is held by Terraform instead: [[zpa.terraform.resource-constraints:ba-certificate-blob-not-sensitive]].

checks.do: Whether a masked read (ZIdentity secrets) is being treated as a source of the secret; only the create response can carry it.

zia-admin-password.statement: The Go SDK's ZIA admin user model says the password is mandatory for POST requests when admin single sign-on is disabled and is not provided in a GET response.

quotes: The admin's password. If admin single sign-on (SSO) is disabled, then this field is mandatory for POST requests. This information is not provided in a GET response.

sandbox-token-send-only.statement: The Go SDK takes the Sandbox submission token from the client configuration, falling back to `ZSCALER_SANDBOX_TOKEN`, and sends it as the `api_token` query parameter on the `/zscsb/submit` and `/zscsb/discan` requests.

sandbox-token-no-read.statement: No API operation returns the Sandbox submission token; it flows only from the client to the request.
sandbox-token-no-read.conditions: Absence from a search: the ZIA OpenAPI paths and the Go and Python SDK sandbox services were searched at their pins for an operation returning a sandbox token; none was found.

obfuscate-flag.statement: The ZIA contract's session read response carries `obfuscateApiKey`, a read-only boolean (default false) described as whether the API key was obfuscated, and no `apiKey` member.

obfuscateApiKey.description: Whether API key was obfuscated or not

cloud-api-key-no-read.statement: No ZIA API operation returns the cloud service API key value; the key is a client-supplied credential.
cloud-api-key-no-read.conditions: Absence from a search: automate-zscaler/openapi/zia.openapi.json was searched at the pin for a path or response property carrying an API key value; only the obfuscateApiKey flag matched.

zid-client-record.statement: The Python SDK's ZIdentity API client record reads name, description, status, accessTokenLifeTime, clientAuthentication, clientResources and id from the response.

quotes: self.name = config["name"] if "name" in config else None
self.description = config["description"] if "description" in config else None
self.status = config["status"] if "status" in config else None
self.client_authentication = config["clientAuthentication"] if "clientAuthentication" in config else None
self.id = config["id"] if "id" in config else None
self.access_token_life_time = config["accessTokenLifeTime"] if "accessTokenLifeTime" in config else None

zid-secrets-masked.statement: GET /api-clients/{id}/secrets lists an API client's secrets with the secret values masked, and applies only when the client's authentication type is SECRET.

expect.description:
Retrieves a list of secrets associated with a specific API client using its ID.

NOTE:

  • Secret values in the response are masked to prevent exposure of sensitive information.
  • This API is applicable only when the authentication type is SECRET.

zid-secret-create.statement: POST /api-clients/{id}/secrets creates a new secret for the client, with no masking note in its description, and its 201 response requires `id`, `createdAt` and `value`, described as the secret value.

expect.description:
Creates and associates a new secret with a specified API client ID. This secret can be used for authentication with Authentication Service.

NOTE: This API is applicable only when the authentication type is SECRET.

zid-full-only-on-create.statement: So the full secret value is available only in the response to creating it; a read of the client or its secrets does not return it.
zid-full-only-on-create.conditions: Rests on the GET secrets description saying values are masked and on the client record carrying no secret field among those the Python model reads; that the create response value is unmasked is inferred from its description lacking the masking note, not shown by a captured response.

ba-cert-no-private-key.statement: The ZPA contract's GET certificate/{certificateId} response for Browser Access certificates has `certificate`, `certChain` and `publicKey` but neither `privateKey` nor the `certBlob` used to upload one.

certificate.description: The certificate text is in PEM format.

expect.description: Adds a certificate with a private key for the specified customer.
